raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Grow the block of padded full attention layers so they fill the unified KV page instead of leaving much of it empty. Fixes #40388.

## Claims

- More KV cache capacity for hybrid models whose full attention page is padded, with `fp8_per_token_head`: Gemma-4-26B +15.8%, Qwen3.6-35B + DFlash +15.6%, Gemma-4-31B + DFlash (TP2) +16.0%.
- Never reserves more KV memory than before: the page, block strides and pool block count are unchanged, and blocks only grow.
- Same outputs in CUDA graph mode: prompt logprobs are identical before and after.
- No throughput regression.
- Models without a padded full attention page are unchanged, including every tested model with plain fp8.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

166 passed, mypy clean. The tests are `cpu_test`s, run by the `v1/core` CPU step in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`. On the base commit, 5 of the new tests fail and 4 pass (the ones checking invariants that already hold). The new tests cover Gemma-4 pth (32/16), a kernel block limit (`MultipleOf(16)` stops at 16), Gemma-4-31B + DFlash TP2 ((32, 32), lcm 32), a Mamba hybrid with a drafter in align and none mode (drafter 416, scheduler block 2912), sliding window and `SinkFullAttentionSpec` keeping their block, and spec-only invariance across `max_model_len`, `max_num_batched_tokens` and async scheduling.

<details>
<summary>New tests on the base commit</summary>

```
$ pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py -rA -k "<new tests>"   # base 7b1d0744, tests only
E       assert 16 == 32
E       assert 16 == 32
E       assert 16 == 416
E       assert 16 == 416
E       assert 16 == 32
PASSED test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_keeps_padded_block_of_other_specs[draft0]
PASSED test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_keeps_padded_block_of_other_specs[draft1]
PASSED test_kv_cache_layer_specs_depend_only_on_specs[4096-2048-False]
PASSED test_kv_cache_layer_specs_depend_only_on_specs[32768-8192-True]
FAILED test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_scales_block_before_padding
FAILED test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_keeps_scheduler_block_with_two_padded_kinds
FAILED test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_keeps_primary_scheduler_block_for_drafter[2912]
FAILED test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_keeps_primary_scheduler_block_for_drafter[262144]
FAILED test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_gemma4_dflash_grows_both_full_kinds
5 failed, 4 passed, 62 deselected in 5.91s
```
</details>

E2E on L40S, KV memory fixed with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`, before and after on the same GPUs. No CI step loads these checkpoints at this size, so capacity and accuracy were validated outside CI.

KV cache capacity (tokens, `fp8_per_token_head`, `--max-model-len 32768`, startup log):

| Model | KV memory | Before | After | Block sizes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gemma-4-26B | 12 GiB | 169,310 | 196,111 (+15.8%) | full 16 → 32 |
| Qwen3.6-35B + DFlash | 4 GiB | 58,415 | 67,502 (+15.6%) | target full 2192 → 4384 |
| Gemma-4-31B + DFlash (TP2) | 8 GiB | 51,830 | 60,132 (+16.0%) | target / drafter full 16 → 32 |

gpt-oss-20b, Gemma-3-12B, Qwen3.5-9B and Nemotron-3-Nano have identical capacity and block sizes before and after. With plain fp8, all tested models are unchanged.

Accuracy:
- Prompt logprobs (`prompt_logprobs`) over a fixed 30k-token text are identical in CUDA graph mode (Gemma-4-26B, Gemma-4-31B + DFlash).
- DFlash acceptance length: 1.857 → 1.854.

Prefix caching with this block structure (Qwen3.6 + DFlash, plain fp8, TP2, target block 2x the Mamba block): outputs of 8 prompts sharing a 20k-token prefix are identical with caching on and off, with 80% of prompt tokens hit.

<details>
<summary>Throughput (single run, random 1024/256, 200 prompts)</summary>

```
vllm serve <model> --kv-cache-dtype fp8_per_token_head --max-model-len 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes <12 GiB Gemma-4, 3 GiB Qwen3.6>  # Qwen3.6: + DFlash, --max-num-seqs 8
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \
  --num-prompts 200 --max-concurrency 16 --ignore-eos --seed 0
```

| Model | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gemma-4-26B | 598 → 610 | 521 → 439 ms | 24.10 → 23.91 ms |
| Qwen3.6-35B + DFlash | 181 → 184 | 19.2 → 18.9 s | 10.48 → 10.43 ms |

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** In hybrid models all layers share one KV block pool, so `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` gives every layer the same physical page. A layer whose page does not divide the largest one keeps its block size and pads its page up. The padding repeats on every block, and for full attention it grows with the context length. It shows up whenever per-token sizes stop being integer multiples of each other, e.g. per-token-head KV scales, head dims that are not powers of two, or a drafter with a different head layout. Gemma-4 with `fp8_per_token_head` leaves about half of every full attention page empty.

**Change.** The page stays as is, and padded full attention layers grow their block to the largest multiple that still fits. For Gemma-4, full attention goes from block 16 to 32 and the padding per page drops from 33,536 B to 512 B, the block structure plain fp8 already uses. The existing loop only records which layers it padded; `_grown_block_sizes` then adjusts those. This follows the sliding window block choice in `attention.py` and the hidden-state block choice, applied to padded full attention.

**Everything else stays as before: the stored KV values, the page layout and every other layer are unchanged, and models without a padded full attention page take the existing path.**

**Rules.**
- Only plain `FullAttentionSpec` grows. Other specs, including full attention subclasses, may tie their block size to a model constant (e.g. Inkling's conv state, static sinks).
- A padded page cannot be split into kernel blocks, so a grown block must run as one kernel block.
- The scheduler block (lcm of group block sizes) may grow only up to the larger of the largest chosen block and its value without growth, so block sizes stay multiples of each other. With several grown specs the combination is chosen jointly: Gemma-4-31B + DFlash picks (32, 32) instead of (32, 48), whose lcm would be 96.
- The result depends only on the KV cache specs, so prefill and decode instances with the same parallel layout agree on the layout.

**Alternatives.** Growing the page and padding sliding window layers instead can save more in some configurations, but which choice is cheaper depends on `max_model_len` and batch settings. Those often differ between prefill and decode instances, and KV connectors need both sides to use the same layout, so the page stays fixed.

**Limitations.**
- OffloadingConnector with `block_size` in `kv_connector_extra_config` requires all groups to share one block size, so it now fails for padded hybrids such as Gemma-4 pth, as plain fp8 already does. `blocks_per_chunk` works.
- Prefix cache hits align to the scheduler block, which can grow (Gemma-4: 16 → 32). Plain fp8 already uses the same block structure.
- Sliding window layers are not grown, so models where a sliding window page is the padded one see no change.

---

Hi @ivanium, could you take a look when you get a chance? This is the follow-up to #40388. The change is small and only touches `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size`.

Another case this covers, from Intel XPU (Arc Pro B70): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash (K=7) with `int8_per_token_head` KV on TRITON_ATTN. The target's full-attention layers (2 KV heads × 520 B per token) end up at block 2176, set by the GDN page, while the drafter's full-attention page (8 heads × 264 B) is 4,595,712 B. The ratio is 2.03, so on main each target page is padded to the drafter's and 49% of every target block is padding.

We have been running an equivalent local change (take the integer multiple of the block that fits, then pad). It moves the target block 2176 → 4352, which leaves 1.5% padding. Walking `_grown_block_sizes` by hand for these specs gives the same 4352: candidates (4352, 2176) for the target, both drafter specs stay at 2176, and the lcm stays at 4352. TRITON_ATTN declares only `MultipleOf(16)`, so `block_stride_alignment` stays `None` and the kernel-block cap doesn't apply. In our deployment the reported KV cache went from ~212K to ~401K tokens with the change. The pool size was not identical between those two boots, so take the ratio as approximate; per token of context the target's pool cost halves.

I haven't run this branch on the GPU yet; I'll report back if it doesn't reproduce our block once it's in our tree.

+1 from B70. We need this behaviour and carry our own equivalent (integer block multiple first, then pad) in our engine kit (https://github.com/Lumnus/b70-flash-next), because int8 per-token-head KV next to a DFlash drafter gives a page ratio of about 2.03, and padding alone loses about half of each target page. On Qwen3.6-35B that was roughly 212K → 401K KV tokens. We'd retire ours for this. My report-back from running your branch still stands.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to draft this comment.

files.patch:
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
 # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
 import copy
+import math
 import mmap
 import subprocess
 import sys
@@ -30,6 +31,7 @@
 from vllm.config.attention import HiSparseConfig
 from vllm.platforms import current_platform
 from vllm.utils.mem_constants import GiB_bytes
+from vllm.v1.attention.backend import MultipleOf
 from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning import (
     check_enough_kv_cache_memory,
     estimate_max_model_len,
@@ -56,6 +58,7 @@
     KVCacheTensor,
     MambaSpec,
     MLAAttentionSpec,
+    SinkFullAttentionSpec,
     SlidingWindowMLASpec,
     SlidingWindowSpec,
     SparseCacheRole,
@@ -1747,6 +1750,187 @@ def test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_uses_padding_for_non_divisible_sizes():
     assert unified_draft_spec.page_size_bytes == target_spec.page_size_bytes
 
 
+def test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_scales_block_before_padding():
+    """Per-token-head scales add 8 B per head, so Gemma 4's full layers (2 heads
+    x 1032 B) no longer divide its SWA page (8 heads x 520 B). The padded full
+    block should hold as many tokens as fit, like the fp8 2:1 case does."""
+    full = replace(
+        new_kv_cache_spec(num_kv_heads=2, head_size=512, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+        state_content_bytes=2 * 512 + 8,
+    )
+    swa = replace(
+        new_sliding_window_spec(
+            num_kv_heads=8, head_size=256, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        ),
+        state_content_bytes=2 * 256 + 8,
+    )
+    unify = kv_cache_planning.unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size
+
+    unified = unify({"full": full, "swa": swa})
+    assert unified["swa"] == swa
+    assert unified["full"].block_size == 32
+    assert unified["full"].page_size_bytes == swa.page_size_bytes
+
+    # Padded pages cannot be split, so a 16-token-max kernel keeps 16.
+    fixed_kernel = replace(full, block_stride_alignment=MultipleOf(16))
+    assert unify({"full": fixed_kernel, "swa": swa})["full"].block_size == 16
+
+    # 80 and 64 fit too, but only 48 keeps the scheduler LCM at 48.
+    swa_48 = replace(swa, block_size=48, state_content_bytes=440)
+    assert unify({"full": full, "swa": swa_48})["full"].block_size == 48
+
+
+def test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_keeps_scheduler_block_with_two_padded_kinds():
+    """Two padded full attention kinds (a target and a drafter) can each grow
+    to a multiple of the largest-page block yet reach a large lcm together (48
+    and 32 give 96). The pair is chosen as a whole, so the scheduler block
+    stays at the largest chosen block."""
+    swa = replace(
+        new_sliding_window_spec(num_kv_heads=1, sliding_window=128),
+        state_content_bytes=1000,
+    )
+    full = replace(new_kv_cache_spec(num_kv_heads=1), state_content_bytes=330)
+    draft = replace(new_kv_cache_spec(num_kv_heads=1), state_content_bytes=490)
+
+    unified = kv_cache_planning.unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size(
+        {"swa": swa, "full": full, "draft": draft}
+    )
+
+    assert unified["full"].block_size == 32
+    assert unified["draft"].block_size == 32
+    assert all(s.page_size_bytes == swa.page_size_bytes for s in unified.values())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mamba_block_size", [2912, 262144])
+def test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_keeps_primary_scheduler_block_for_drafter(
+    mamba_block_size,
+):
+    """A bf16 drafter next to a hybrid nvfp4 target: 816 tokens would
+    fill the page best but make the scheduler block 148,512. 416 divides the
+    primary 2912-token block, so the scheduler block stays 2912. Without
+    prefix caching the Mamba block is max_model_len; it must not lift the
+    bound or make the plan depend on it."""
+    full = replace(
+        new_kv_cache_spec(block_size=2912, num_kv_heads=1), state_content_bytes=1152
+    )
+    mamba = new_mamba_spec(
+        block_size=mamba_block_size, page_size_padded=full.page_size_bytes
+    )
+    draft = replace(new_kv_cache_spec(num_kv_heads=1), state_content_bytes=4096)
+
+    unified = kv_cache_planning.unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size(
+        {"full": full, "mamba": mamba, "draft": draft}
+    )
+
+    assert unified["full"] == full
+    assert unified["mamba"] == mamba
+    assert unified["draft"].block_size == 416
+    assert unified["draft"].page_size_bytes == full.page_size_bytes
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "draft",
+    [
+        new_sliding_window_spec(num_kv_heads=1, sliding_window=2048),
+        SinkFullAttentionSpec(
+            block_size=16,
+            num_kv_heads=1,
+            head_size=64,
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+            sink_len=64,
+        ),
+    ],
+)
+def test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_keeps_padded_block_of_other_specs(draft):
+    """Only plain full attention grows before padding; other specs may tie their
+    block size to a model constant (e.g. Inkling's conv state, static sinks)."""
+    full = replace(
+        new_kv_cache_spec(block_size=2912, num_kv_heads=1), state_content_bytes=1152
+    )
+    draft = replace(draft, state_content_bytes=4096)
+

+    fp8_per_token_head: content is K + V data plus one fp32 scale each."""
+
+    def pth(spec, head_size):
+        return replace(spec, state_content_bytes=2 * head_size + 8)

+    fp8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    swa = pth(

+        ),

+    draft_swa = pth(

+        ),

+    )
+    draft_full = pth(new_kv_cache_spec(num_kv_heads=4, head_size=128, dtype=fp8), 128)
+    specs = {f"swa.{i}": swa for i in range(50)}
+    specs |= {f"full.{i}": full for i in range(10)}
+    specs |= {f"draft_swa.{i}": draft_swa for i in range(4)}

+def test_unify_kv_cache_page_size_gemma4_dflash_grows_both_full_kinds():

+    would grow to 32 and 48 (lcm 96); together they take 32 and 32, so the

+def _grown_block_sizes(
+    kv_cache_spec: dict[str, KVCacheSpec],
+    padded_layer_names: set[str],
+    max_page_size: int,
+) -> dict[str, int]:
+    """Grown block sizes for the padded full attention layers of
+    ``kv_cache_spec``, whose pages are already unified to ``max_page_size``.
+
+    Each takes the largest multiple of its block whose page still fits and
+    that fits one kernel block, since padded pages are never split; other
+    layers keep their block. The scheduler block (lcm of all block sizes) may
+    grow up to the larger of the largest chosen block and the lcm without
+    growth, but not further, so block sizes that are not multiples of each other
+    cannot inflate it. The result depends only on the specs.
+    """
+    if not padded_layer_names:
+        return {}
+    # Keyed by padding too: only padded layers grow.
+    layer_names_by_key: dict[tuple[KVCacheSpec, bool], list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
+    for layer_name, spec in kv_cache_spec.items():
+        # Mamba block sizes never change and can equal max_model_len, so
+        # Mamba stays out of the lcm below.
+        if not isinstance(spec, MambaSpec):
+            key = (spec, layer_name in padded_layer_names)
+            layer_names_by_key[key].append(layer_name)
+
+    # Candidate block sizes per key, largest first; the last is the block size
+    # without growth.
+    candidates: dict[tuple[KVCacheSpec, bool], list[int]] = {}
+    for spec, padded in layer_names_by_key:
+        grown: list[int] = []
+        # Only plain full attention grows; other specs, including full attention
+        # subclasses, may tie their block size to a model constant (e.g.
+        # Inkling's conv state, static sinks).
+        if padded and type(spec) is FullAttentionSpec:
+            # A padded page cannot be split into kernel blocks, so the block
+            # must divide alignment.base (see get_block_stride_alignment); an
+            # int alignment is in bytes.
+            alignment = spec.block_stride_alignment
+            max_kernel_block = (
+                None
+                if alignment is None or isinstance(alignment, int)
+                else alignment.base
+            )
+            block_size = 2 * spec.block_size
+            while (max_kernel_block is None or block_size <= max_kernel_block) and (
+                spec.copy_with_new_block_size(block_size).unpadded_page_size_bytes
+                <= max_page_size
+            ):
+                if max_kernel_block is None or max_kernel_block % block_size == 0:
+                    grown.append(block_size)
+                block_size += spec.block_size
+        candidates[spec, padded] = [*reversed(grown), spec.block_size]
+    if all(len(block_sizes) == 1 for block_sizes in candidates.values()):
+        return {}
+
+    def largest_dividing(bound: int) -> list[int] | None:
+        """Each key's largest candidate dividing ``bound``, if all have one."""
+        chosen: list[int] = []
+        for block_sizes in candidates.values():
+            fitting = [b for b in block_sizes if bound % b == 0]
+            if not fitting:
+                return None
+            chosen.append(fitting[0])
+        return chosen
+
+    base_lcm = math.lcm(*(block_sizes[-1] for block_sizes in candidates.values()))
+    all_block_sizes = {b for block_sizes in candidates.values() for b in block_sizes}
+    best_rank: tuple[Fraction, int] | None = None
+    best_block_sizes: list[int] = []
+    # Candidates are multiples of the block without growth, so lcm(chosen) >=
+    # base_lcm, and lcm(chosen) <= max(base_lcm, *chosen) holds exactly when
+    # every chosen block divides a bound in {base_lcm} | candidates. Try only
+    # those, each key taking its largest candidate that divides the bound.
+    for bound in sorted(all_block_sizes | {base_lcm}):
+        chosen = largest_dividing(bound)
+        if chosen is None:
+            continue
+        scheduler_block_size = math.lcm(*chosen)
+        if scheduler_block_size > max(base_lcm, *chosen):
+            continue
+        # Fewest blocks per token of context, then the finer scheduler block.
+        # Approximate: weights by layer count, not by the padded groups the
+        # pool charges.
+        blocks_per_token = sum(
+            (
+                Fraction(len(layer_names_by_key[key]), b)
+                for key, b in zip(candidates, chosen, strict=True)
+            ),
+            start=Fraction(0),
+        )
+        rank = (blocks_per_token, scheduler_block_size)
+        if best_rank is None or rank < best_rank:
+            best_rank, best_block_sizes = rank, chosen
+    assert best_rank is not None, "the block sizes without growth always qualify"
+
+    grown_block_sizes: dict[str, int] = {}
+    for (spec, padded), block_size in zip(candidates, best_block_sizes, strict=True):
+        if block_size == spec.block_size:
+            continue
+        assert isinstance(spec, AttentionSpec)
+        layer_names = layer_names_by_key[spec, padded]
+        natural_page_size = spec.copy_with_new_block_size(
+            block_size
+        ).unpadded_page_size_bytes
+        wasted_bytes = max_page_size - natural_page_size
+        logger.info_once(
+            "Using block size %d instead of %d for %d full attention layers "
+            "(e.g. %s); page padding wastes %d bytes (%.2f%%) per block",
+            block_size,
+            spec.block_size,
+            len(layer_names),
+            layer_names[0],
+            wasted_bytes,
+            wasted_bytes / max_page_size * 100,
+        )
+        grown_block_sizes.update(dict.fromkeys(layer_names, block_size))
+    return grown_block_sizes
+
+

     kv_cache_spec: dict[str, KVCacheSpec],
 ) -> dict[str, KVCacheSpec]:

Hi @ivanium, could you take a look when you get a chance? This is the follow-up to #40388. The change is small and only touches `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size`.

Another case this covers, from Intel XPU (Arc Pro B70): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash (K=7) with `int8_per_token_head` KV on TRITON_ATTN. The target's full-attention layers (2 KV heads × 520 B per token) end up at block 2176, set by the GDN page, while the drafter's full-attention page (8 heads × 264 B) is 4,595,712 B. The ratio is 2.03, so on main each target page is padded to the drafter's and 49% of every target block is padding.

We have been running an equivalent local change (take the integer multiple of the block that fits, then pad). It moves the target block 2176 → 4352, which leaves 1.5% padding. Walking `_grown_block_sizes` by hand for these specs gives the same 4352: candidates (4352, 2176) for the target, both drafter specs stay at 2176, and the lcm stays at 4352. TRITON_ATTN declares only `MultipleOf(16)`, so `block_stride_alignment` stays `None` and the kernel-block cap doesn't apply. In our deployment the reported KV cache went from ~212K to ~401K tokens with the change. The pool size was not identical between those two boots, so take the ratio as approximate; per token of context the target's pool cost halves.

I haven't run this branch on the GPU yet; I'll report back if it doesn't reproduce our block once it's in our tree.
